messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Data for SEM lavaan
parts:
Marzhan,
I am not a statistician but there is no inherent connection between data collection method (e.g. survey) and the appropriateness of SEM.  The salient data feature with SEM is typically the distribution.  When counts are large, into 3 digits, my understanding is that the normal distribution offers an adequate approximation to count data.  When counts are smaller, they follow a Poisson distribution and, like dichotomous data, the mean is not independent of the variance.  Also similar to dichotomous data, none of that really matters if the variable in question is exogenous because estimation is conditional on exogenous variables.  If you are not estimating mean structures and you use a robust estimator, that may suffice for an endogenous count variable with smaller counts.  You might also investigate whether a log transformation of a small count is of use.  Others may be able to elaborate, clarify or offer references.

Keith
